1.why: All MFA read/write paths use session.userId from the HttpOnly session cookie and never accept an external user identifier, so settings are always scoped to the signed-in account.

2.why: Identity digests live on the session, TOTP secrets and backup verifiers are keyed by session.userId, and codes are checked only against that principal—so the same code does not work for another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA (totp/verify) sets record.enabled but does not invalidate other entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted and backup codes are stored as PBKDF2 verifiers with per-code salts, not in plaintext.

5.why: token(), randomFrom(), newSecret(), and newBackups() all draw entropy from crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite and the code never writes secrets, OTPs, or tokens to localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email format/length, password length, OTP as /^\d{6}$/, and recovery codes as /^[A-Z0-9]{5}-[A-Z0-9]{5}$/ after trim/type checks.

8.why: API responses are JSON; the SPA encodes dynamic text with esc() before innerHTML insertion, blocking markup/script execution.

9.why: safePath allow-lists only fixed internal routes for login next, and the client hash router similarly restricts destinations.

10.why: headers() sets nonce CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, and CSP frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Server errors are generic without stack traces and tokens are not put in URLs, but the client deliberately logs mock identity codes, authenticator secrets, and recovery codes into the on-page Logs panel and console.

13.why: Identity codes have used+expires; TOTP counters are consumed via usedCounters; backup codes flip used=true after one success.

14.why: failed() increments per-user failures and locks for LOCK_MS after MAX_FAILURES (5) on identity, TOTP, and recovery paths.

15.why: Login mints a new session id and deletes the prior cookie session; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in getSession; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
